episodes.210739: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward across Lake Ontario, southern ON, and southern Lower MI toward Lake Erie during the early afternoon through late evening of the 31st. Ahead of the front, several lines of multicell thunderstorms and a discrete supercell persisted generally eastward across northern OH during the late afternoon through the late evening of the 31st. Some of these storms produced sporadic straight-line convective wind damage, two mesovortex-related tornadoes, and small hail. The ambient environment of these storms included weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. It appears the development of a southwesterly to west-southwesterly low-level jet and resulting enhanced surface-based ESRH coinciding with favorably-low mixed layer LCL's contributed to the development of the two tornadoes.
episodes.210753: Elevated thunderstorms developed north of a warm front Thursday night (3/30) across central Wisconsin and east-central Wisconsin. These storms tracked eastward across the region through the early morning hours on Friday (3/31).  The strongest storms produced large hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.210773: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northeast Illinois during the late evening of March 30th producing large hail.
episodes.210774: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the morning of March 31st producing isolated large hail.
episodes.210797: A boundary set up across eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania allowed for ample lift ahead of the cold frontal passage given sufficient instability and ample shear in place across the region during the afternoon and evening hours of March 31, 2026. These thunderstorms began to develop across western Ohio and gradually developed stronger as they continued tracking across central and eastern Ohio and into portions of western Pennsylvania. This line of thunderstorms along the boundary caused multiple instances of tree damage across Warren and McKean counties with no injuries reported despite all of the tree damage. A secondary surge of thunderstorms later in the evening allowed for a tree to get knocked down in Clearfield County, with no injuries reported from this incident.
episodes.210965: A line of elevated thunderstorms tracked through central and east-central Wisconsin during the middle to late part of the morning on Friday (3/31) north of a semi-stationary boundary.  The strongest storms produced hail up to nickel size.
episodes.210966: Thunderstorms produced large hail over the bay of Green Bay during the overnight hours on Thursday (3/30).
episodes.211001: Both on the evening of the 30th and late afternoon of the 31st, the southeast TX Panhandle was impacted by severe storms that formed as a small complex. Each day looked very similar on radar. These storms produced wind gusts up to 64 mph and hail up to the size of quarters on the 30th. On the 31st the storms did produce hail up to quarters but no wind gusts were recorded.
episodes.211028: On Tuesday, March 31st, warm, moisture-rich Gulf air surged into the Northeast ahead of a nearly stationary front, placing the region in a favorable warm-sector environment for severe thunderstorms.  The combination of greater instability, strong wind shear, and abundant moisture ultimately led to severe thunderstorms Tuesday afternoon and evening. Daytime clearing likely increased instability, while both cooler incoming air and strong winds aloft supported organized storms capable of producing large hail, and damaging winds.
episodes.211054: Decaying convection from across the eastern Texas Panhandle produced several heat burst episodes across western Oklahoma during the mid to late evening of the 30th into the 31st.
episodes.211055: On the afternoon of the 30th, a dryline moved back into the Rolling Plains of West Texas allowing for low level moisture to surge into the region. Areas on the caprock saw scattered high based showers and thunderstorms generating severe wind gusts over Lubbock and Floyd Counties. Stronger moisture in the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle allowed for more robust thunderstorms. These storms produced severe wind gusts as well as hail as large as golf ball size in the city of Memphis (Hall County).
episodes.211057: A dryline emerged over the Rolling Plains on the afternoon of the 31st. At the same time, a cold front was moving southward which generated strong thunderstorms at the intersection of these two features. This activity initially formed over the southeastern Texas Panhandle and moved southward into the Rolling Plains during the evening hours. These storms produced a mix of large hail up to golf ball size along with severe wind gusts up to 68 mph.
episodes.211086: On March 31st, severe thunderstorms moved across Lake Erie and into portions of southwestern New York as a potent shortwave trough crossed the area with a stationary front draped across the south shore of Lake Ontario and lake breeze boundaries found across the area. Shear values of 40+ knots and instability values of around 1,000 J/kg at the time the trough crossed the area combined for a favorable setup for severe thunderstorms. The thunderstorms caused a tornado, damaging winds, flash flooding and significant hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.211582: Thunderstorms moving across eastern Iowa produced hail up to the size of pennies as they moved across eastern Iowa during the early morning hours in Johnson and Scott Counties.
episodes.211583: Morning thunderstorms  moving across eastern Iowa south of Interstate 80 intensified and produced hail that ranged from 1.00 to 1.25 inches as the storms moved east. Rainfall amounts ranged from a half an inch to an inch.
episodes.211584: Morning thunderstorms  moved from eastern Iowa into northwest Illinois south of Interstate 80 and intensified producing hail that ranged from a quarter to golf ball sized hail as the storms during the morning. Rainfall amounts ranged from a half an inch to an inch.
episodes.211586: Showers and thunderstorms moved across far northwest Illinois during the evening of March 30th.  One of these thunderstorms produced damaging thunderstorm winds near the US Army Depot near Savanna.
episodes.211759: Ahead of a southeastward moving cold front, broken lines of showers and thunderstorms developed in the evening hours. A surge of mid 70s temperatures with upper 50s dew points resulted in sufficient destabilization with MLCAPE up to 1000 J/kg, effective shear of 30-40 knots, and a gradient of 700-900 DCAPE. This allowed for some thunderstorms to become severe with large hail and damaging wind as the result, including two measured 58 mph gusts in southwest Pennsylvania.
episodes.211835: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a warm front over southern WI. Large hail was reported with one of the thunderstorms.
episodes.211836: Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a slow moving cold front over southern WI. Some large hail reports were received from east central WI.
episodes.211852: Clusters of thunderstorms formed west of the I-55 corridor on the morning of March 31, 2026, in advance of an upper level disturbance. Several of these thunderstorms produced hail, the largest of which was golf ball sized in Mason County.
episodes.212059: Warm and humid air to the south of a warm frontal boundary spawned heavy rain producing thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Storms repeatedly moving over the same regions produced pockets of 3 to 4 inches of rain which triggered areas of flash flooding.
episodes.212112: On March 31st, strong to severe thunderstorms moved across Lake Erie and into portions of southwestern New York as a potent shortwave trough crossed the area with a stationary front draped across the south shore of Lake Ontario and lake breeze boundaries were found across the area. Shear values of 40+ knots and instability values of around 1,000 J/kg at the time the trough crossed the area combined for a favorable setup for severe thunderstorms. The thunderstorms caused a tornado, damaging winds, flash flooding and significant hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.212162: Elevated southerly winds continued to transport moisture across the Mid-South. Strong daytime heating yielded plentiful sunshine, driving instability values to around 1000 J/kg across north Mississippi. Though convective coverage remained sparse, an isolated cell managed to tap into the available instability just before sunset.
episodes.212247: Thunderstorms brought large hail and damaging winds to parts of lower Michigan on late March 30 into the early hours of March 31.
episodes.212309: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward across Lake Ontario, southern ON, and southern Lower MI toward Lake Erie during the early afternoon through late evening of the 31st. Ahead of the front, a line of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward and generated isolated straight-line convective wind damage in Erie County during the early evening of the 31st. The ambient environment of these storms included moderate to strong effective bulk shear and weak MUCAPE.
episodes.212310: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward across Lake Ontario, southern ON, and southern Lower MI toward Lake Erie during the early afternoon through late evening of the 31st. Ahead of the front, a line of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward along and near the OH shore of Lake Erie and generated sporadic peak straight-line convective wind gusts of storm-to-hurricane-force during the late afternoon through early evening of the 31st. The ambient environment of these storms included moderate to strong effective bulk shear and weak to moderate MUCAPE.
episodes.212411: Storms moved across the area on the evening of the 30th into the early morning hours of the 31st, producing a couple rounds of heavy rain and several reports of accumulating hail, with hailstones as large as ping pong balls.
episodes.212429: Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a slow moving cold front over southern WI.

An EF1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 100-mph impacted the Chesterland area. Radar data indicate this was a rare anticyclonic tornado. The tornado began just northeast of the intersection of Watt Road and Fairmount Road, where a large barn had its roof collapse. As the tornado moved generally eastward, it downed several large pine trees onto a house along Fairmount Road, about halfway between Watt and Sperry Roads, but there was no obvious damage to the home. A power pole was snapped in half at this same location. Farther east along Fairmount Road, the tornado downed additional large pine trees. One of the trees fell onto a home and caused some roof and gutter damage. The tornado ended soon thereafter, just west-northwest of the intersection of Fairmount and Rockhaven Roads.
